items.description:
All these tools do the same core thing: transcribe your speech and paste it wherever your cursor is. The differences come down to platform, engine preference, and how much you want beyond basic dictation.
A few starting points:

items.title: Cross-platform default: Handy
items.description: . Biggest open-source project in this list, runs on Linux, macOS, and Windows.

items.title: On macOS, want a native feel: VoiceInk
Want cloud providers or AI transformations on top: Whispering
Just Tell Me What to Use

items.description: : means on-device speech recognition. means the tool supports both local and cloud or BYO-cloud setups.
items.title: Directory

items.description: Speech recognition engines, models, and APIs that power the tools listed above.

items.title: whisper.cpp
items.description: Pure C/C++ Whisper inference with zero dependencies; runs on Apple Silicon, CUDA, Vulkan, and WASM.

items.title: Faster Whisper
items.description: CTranslate2-based Whisper reimplementation; up to 4x faster with lower memory.

items.title: Vosk
items.description: Lightweight offline ASR with compact models, 20+ languages, and multi-language bindings.

items.title: WhisperKit
items.description: Swift package for on-device Whisper on Apple Silicon with streaming support.

items.title: Awesome Whisper
items.description: Curated list of Whisper tools and resources.
